title: Potential Asset Rotations: Deep Dive Analysis
summary: Liquidity, recession risk, and foreign-asset rotation.
coverage_note: All text and image labels read. Includes issuance mechanics, labor/recession thesis, politics/privacy, ETF flows, Ethereum positioning, capital flows, refinancing, valuation rotation and gold. Quoted Miran/Roubini numerical equivalents explicitly disclaimed by author, so not counted as her forecasts. Historical 2019 error acknowledged, not a new call.

evidence.title: 2024 preliminary payroll benchmark
evidence.finding: Preliminary March 2024 nonfarm level revision was -818,000; this was not the final revision.

claims.reason: Unemployment stayed around 4-4.5% through 2025 rather than showing a typical deep-recession surge. The economy did not need to enter recession for that mild path; fiscal/structural labor causality remains unproven.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify the proposed causal mechanism.

evidence.title: Unemployment rate
evidence.finding: Latest-vintage data: December 2024 4.1%; November 2025 4.5%; December 2025 4.4%. Download capped November 7 2026.

claims.next_check: Check monthly peak and labor-force composition; identify fiscal contribution separately.

claims.reason: At least by some metrics does not specify a recession rule or window. Latest-vintage real GDP grew 3.2% and 2.4% annualized in 2024 Q3/Q4 and remained positive each 2025 quarter, substantial counterevidence to an imminent broad contraction. Do not count that as a successful mild recession merely because selected sectors were weak.
claims.mechanism_assessment: Outcome evidence does not independently identify the proposed causal mechanism.

evidence.title: Real GDP growth
evidence.finding: 2024 Q3/Q4: 3.2%, 2.4%; 2025 Q1-Q4: 0.1%, 4.0%, 3.9%, 0.2%, annualized latest-vintage observations.

claims.next_check: Keep sector contractions separate from broad recession; obtain original definition before binary scoring.

claims.reason: Different nominal growth rates require sector-specific deflators. Construction stimulus plausibly matters, but the heatmap alone does not identify the IRA contribution.

evidence.finding: July 23-August 2 2024 ETHE outflows sum $2,116.5 m; aggregate all-fund flows sum -$511.2 m. Table begins July 23, not June 23.

framework_lessons: Separate accounting, prices, and policy intent.
assessment: The article explicitly withholds endorsement of quoted rate-equivalence estimates and admits an earlier rotation miss. Its strongest verified points are ETF outflows, employment revision risk, continued privacy enforcement, and 2025 Fed purchases. Broad recession and rotation language is flexible; positive GDP and uneven foreign returns resist an uncomplicated win. Source launch-date and ratio-scale errors are preserved as editorial limitations.
verification_limitations: Current snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date vintage.
Image labels were inventoried; chart images were not inspected.
No portfolio or equity total returns are inferred from business results.
